subject: fix(windows): pin the subprocess READ decoder to UTF-8 (the mirror of #4658) (#4674)
what: Fixed pin the subprocess READ decoder to UTF-8 (the mirror of #4658) (#4674).
why:
What was broken, in plain English: when one GRIP process runs another and
captures its output, it was letting the operating system guess how to turn the
child's bytes back into text. On Windows that guess is cp1252, not UTF-8, so a
check mark or a box-drawing character came back as three pieces of nonsense.
Nothing crashed and the exit code stayed 0 -- the parent just quietly believed
the wrong string.

subject: fix(tests): 10 of GRIP's 14 Windows CI failures were test bugs, not product bugs (#4704)
what: Fixed 10 of GRIP's 14 Windows CI failures were test bugs, not product bugs (#4704).
why:
What this does in plain English: three of GRIP's Windows tests were failing on
the Windows CI runner even though the code they test is correct. Two of them
checked a file path by looking for the text "bin/python" at the end of it --
but Windows writes paths with backslashes, so the check never matched there no
matter how right the code was. They now compare the path's components instead,
which reads the same on every operating system. The third test exercises a
macOS-only scheduler that has no Windows equivalent at all, so it is now
skipped on Windows with the reason written down.

subject: fix(gates): the zsh colon-modifier gate only covered refspecs, so a git show returned four false zeros (#4706)
what: Fixed the zsh colon-modifier gate only covered refspecs, so a git show returned four false zeros (#4706).
why:
What this does in plain English: zsh quietly eats the character right after a
variable name followed by a colon, treating it as a formatting instruction. GRIP
already guarded the one place this was known to bite -- git push refspecs -- but
the same trap exists everywhere. Tonight a `git show` of a file at a commit came
back empty four times running, and the emptiness was read as "the file does not
contain that", when the command had never addressed the file at all. The guard
now covers the general shape, so it fails loudly instead of lying quietly.

subject: fix(tests): a red-on-main gate test was pinning an implementation detail, not a property (#4712)
what: Fixed a red-on-main gate test was pinning an implementation detail, not a property (#4712).
why:
What this does in plain English: one test in the gate suite has been failing on
main. Nothing was broken. The test checked that GRIP's environment-variable
patterns were a specific Python type, and someone later made them compile lazily
to save startup time — a correct optimisation that changed the type. The test
now checks what actually matters: that each pattern works as a matcher.

subject: fix(tests): five assertions in one file could not fail, including one named "should not hang" (#4715)
what: Fixed five assertions in one file could not fail, including one named "should not hang" (#4715).
why:
What this does in plain English: five checks in this test file were written so
they could never fail. Three said `assert True`, which checks nothing at all.
Two were sneakier — `assert X or True` reads like a real check, but anything
followed by "or true" is always true. So the file reported twenty-four passing
tests while five of them were watching nothing. Each now checks the thing its
own name promises, and each was proven able to fail before being trusted.

subject: fix(hooks): stop the bash-error learner persisting credentials, and tell the truth about its wiring (#4802)
what: Fixed stop the bash-error learner persisting credentials, and tell the truth about its wiring (#4802).
why:
What this does, in plain English. GRIP has a hook that watches every Bash

is not repeated. That note included the failed command itself, word for word.
If the command happened to contain a credential -- a curl with an Authorization
header, a secret in front of a script -- that credential was written into
learning/insights.jsonl and broadcast to the other machines. That file is
tracked in git and is not encrypted.

subject: fix: three silent breakages — unreadable skill descriptions, fatal startup abort, unrenderable brand variant (#4836)
what: Fixed three silent breakages — unreadable skill descriptions, fatal startup abort, unrenderable brand variant (#4836).
why:
closeout, converge, dojo, mem, mesh and osa each opened with a shebang on
line 1 and wrapped the whole document in a `: <<'MARKDOWN'` heredoc, so they
were valid bash and valid markdown at once. Claude Code's skill loader reads
frontmatter only when `---` is the first line, so for all six it fell back to
the directory name and took the first body line as the description. Every one
of them advertised itself to the model as the literal string
"#!/usr/bin/env bash" -- verifiable in any session's skill listing. /converge
and /mesh are CLAUDE.md headline commands, so two of the most advertised
skills in GRIP were among the unreadable ones.

subject: fix(preload): an abandoned recall was not abandoned, it was joined at exit (#4842)
what: Fixed an abandoned recall was not abandoned, it was joined at exit (#4842).
why:

that 'an abandoned worker thread is harmless'. It is not. Pool workers are
NON-daemon and concurrent.futures.thread registers an atexit handler that
JOINS them, so the interpreter blocks at exit until the recall finishes
regardless of the timeout.

subject: feat: EvidenceState gate — Belnap-Dunn evidence typing with sealed flips (#5019)
what: Added evidenceState gate — Belnap-Dunn evidence typing with sealed flips (#5019).
why:
Adds lib/evidence_state.py: every claim/variable carries a first-class
evidence type {LATENT, TRUE, FALSE, CONFLICT} (Belnap-Dunn bit-pairs) with
genuine FDE propagation, ATMS-style assumption tracking, and a
materiality-sensitive suspension POLICY layered explicitly above the logic
(never blanket suspend-on-unknown). Two-layer store: working state may cycle
back to latent (eviction), the flip ledger is append-only and each
LATENT-to-manifest climb can seal a signed PRECOG IDR leaf (fail-open,
mirroring sovereign_council._seal_idr). Outputs ship finite, versioned
negative provenance — the exact list of declared variables still unobserved
at decision time — and a typed action vocabulary (REQUEST_EVIDENCE,
BOUNDED_SCENARIOS, FILE_UNDER_ASSUMPTION, ESCALATE, SUSPEND) so suspension
is a last resort, not the strategy.

checking bucket == "api-key"; ~/.zshrc, lib/relay_dispatcher.py's

exhaustion.
